promise: How your country works, in plain words
Money, scams and the future, explained
posts.community: Follow and share: an informed Kenya is unstoppable.
posts.caption:
Sasa, Kenya! Jua Kesho is here: politics with receipts, how the country works in plain words, and the money, scams and future that affect you. Jua nchi yako. Drop the one thing about Kenya you wish someone explained properly.

#KenyaOnRecord

posts.line: Every month *4.25%* of our gross pay goes to the housing levy and SHIF before we see it.
posts.fact: Housing levy: 1.5% of gross salary. SHIF: 2.75% of gross salary. Both come off before your net pay.
posts.message: Kenyans pay 4.25% of gross pay to housing and health levies and want to see what it buys.
posts.source: Affordable Housing Act, 2024 (s.4: 1.5% of gross salary); Social Health Insurance Act, 2023 and Social Health Insurance (General) Regulations, 2024 (2.75% of gross salary)
posts.caption:
Check your payslip. 1.5% housing levy + 2.75% SHIF, every month. We pay. One question: what are we getting? 👇🏾

What have you seen from this money? Drop it in the comments.

#HousingLevy #KenyaOnRecord
beats: The housing levy and SHIF take *4.25%* of gross pay.
The housing levy is 1.5% of gross salary.
SHIF takes another 2.75% before your net pay.
Kenyans are asking: what has the money *delivered so far?*
posts.action: Check the levy lines on your payslip, then ask your MP what they bought
posts.impact: Ordinary Kenyans pay for it in taxes and lost services.

posts.title: Turn a 1-hour lecture into notes in *2 minutes*
moves: Record the lecture on your phone (ask the lecturer first).
Upload the audio to an AI that takes voice files, like Gemini.
Ask: “Bullet notes + 5 exam questions, simple English.”
posts.caption:
AI Hack: a 1-hour lecture into clean notes and practice questions in about 2 minutes. Always ask before recording. Send this to the class group before CATs.

#AIHack #KenyaOnRecord

posts.hook: one ballot day, six jobs to fill
posts.title: The *6 votes* you cast on 10 August 2027
moves: President and Governor: lead the national and county governments.
Senator: defends your county's share of national money.
MP and Woman Rep: make national laws and approve the budget.
MCA: makes county laws and checks your governor.
posts.payoff: Know the job before you pick the person.
posts.message: On 10 August 2027 you elect six leaders, each with a different job.
posts.source: Constitution of Kenya 2010, Articles 95, 96, 97, 177, 180, 185; IEBC: general election on 10 August 2027 (standardmedia.co.ke/article/2001551158)
posts.caption:
10 August 2027. Six ballots, one day. We all know the President and the Governor... but what does your MCA actually do? Save this before the campaign noise starts.

Tag a first-time voter.

#Civic101 #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Kenya votes on *10 August 2027*.
You will cast six ballots on that one day.
They are for President, Governor, Senator, MP, Woman Rep and MCA.
Learn what each office does, *then* pick the person.
posts.action: Check you're registered: verify.iebc.or.ke or SMS your ID number to 70000

posts.meaning: What you type to tell an AI what you want. Vague prompt, vague answer. Give it a role, a task and an example.
posts.try_this: Not “write a caption” but “3 funny captions for my thrift reel, Kenyan English, under 12 words”.
posts.caption:
Decode No. 1: Prompt. The difference between a boring AI answer and a fire one is how you ask. Save this, then share your best prompt in the comments.

#Decode #KenyaOnRecord

posts.hook: it comes back every single year
posts.meaning: The yearly law that sets your taxes. Treasury drafts it. MPs vote on it.
posts.try_this: When it's published, read the tax changes on parliament.go.ke and send your views during public participation. That's your right.
posts.message: The Finance Bill decides your taxes every year, and you have a right to be heard on it.
posts.source: Constitution of Kenya 2010, Art. 118 (public participation in Parliament) and Art. 221 (budget estimates); Public Finance Management Act, 2012
posts.caption:
Every year the same story: Finance Bill comes, prices go up, we complain on X. This time we read it first. The Constitution gives us a say before MPs vote.

Share this before it's tabled.

#FinanceBill #KenyaOnRecord
beats: It comes back *every year.*
The Finance Bill sets your taxes.
Treasury drafts. MPs vote.
You have a right to be heard.
Read it. *Speak up.*
posts.action: Read the Bill on parliament.go.ke and send your view to the Finance Committee

posts.claim: You need to know coding to build with AI.
posts.real: Most AI tools take plain English. You can build a bot or a site this weekend without code.
posts.source: General: mainstream AI assistants and no-code automation tools accept plain-language instructions
posts.caption:
Cap or No Cap? “You need coding to build with AI.” CAP. Start with plain English, learn code as you go. Tag the friend who keeps saying “I'm not a tech person”.

#CapOrNoCap #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Many people think you need coding to use AI.
Most AI tools take *plain English* instructions.
You can build a simple bot this weekend.
No code is needed, so *just start.*

posts.title: “Get paid to like TikToks”
posts.sms: Hi! Earn Ksh 2,000 daily liking videos. Pay Ksh 500 registration to start today.
tips: Real jobs never ask you to pay to start.
Nobody pays you just to like posts.
posts.source: Common 'task scam' pattern (pay-to-start online jobs); confirm against a current Communications Authority of Kenya or Safaricom fraud advisory before posting
posts.caption:
"Earn daily for liking TikToks, just pay Ksh 500 to register." That's the scam. Real jobs don't charge you to start.

Send this to the group chat, mtu anahitaji kuiona.

#Usiibiwe #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Some job ads promise pay for liking TikToks.
Then they ask for *Ksh 500* to get started.
That fee is the scam.
Real jobs never ask you to pay.
Send this to someone who is job hunting.

posts.name: M-Pesa
posts.fact: Kenya made sending money by SMS an everyday thing, long before most of the world had heard of mobile money.
posts.now: We started it. The world followed.
posts.caption:
Made in Africa: in 2007 Kenya launched M-Pesa, and sending money by phone became normal here. Which African innovation are you proud of? Drop it in the comments.

#MadeInAfrica #KenyaOnRecord
beats: *M-Pesa* was launched in Kenya in 2007.
It let anyone send money by SMS.
Kenya started it, and *the world followed.*

posts.what: 59% of the Sh515bn for 14 flagship projects was never used, says the Auditor-General.
posts.why: Idle money still costs us: fees on undrawn loans, and projects we never get.
posts.check: Auditor-General reports are public on parliament.go.ke. Read one page tonight.
posts.source: Auditor-General Nancy Gathungu to the National Assembly Budget Committee, 2 June 2025 (Capital FM: capitalfm.africa/audit-exposes-sh304bn-in-idle-govt-project-funds)
posts.caption:
Sh304bn. Idle. Sitting there while loans charge fees. Receipts: the Auditor-General's report 👇🏾

Read it, then share and ask your MP where the projects are.

#FollowTheMoney #KenyaOnRecord
beats: *Sh304bn* for 14 flagship projects was never used.
That is 59% of the Sh515bn set aside, says the Auditor-General.
Undrawn loans still charge us fees.
Read the Auditor-General's report on *parliament.go.ke.*

posts.title: How to spot a *paid hashtag* in 30 seconds
moves: Same phrase, many accounts, same hour? Copy-paste army.
Tap the profiles: new, few real followers, posts only hashtags.
Search the tag, sort by oldest: see who started it and when.
posts.payoff: Some get paid $10–15 a day to trend.
posts.source: Mozilla Foundation, 'Inside the Shadowy World of Disinformation-for-hire in Kenya', Odanga Madung & Brian Obilo, 2 Sept 2021 (mozillafoundation.org/en/blog/fellow-research-inside-the-shadowy-world-of-disinformation-for-hire-in-kenya)
posts.caption:
That hashtag trending this morning? Some trends are bought. Mozilla researchers found influencers paid via M-Pesa to push them. Same words, same hour, fresh accounts.

Check before you retweet. Send this to the group chat that believes every trend.

#SeeThroughIt #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Some trending hashtags are *paid for*.
Some accounts get *$10-15 a day* to push one.
Watch for the same words posted in the same hour.
Look for new accounts with few real followers.
Check before you *share.*

posts.claim: Africa is basically one country with one culture.
posts.who: a stereotype still found in comments
posts.claim_source: Recurring stereotype in comment sections and old textbooks; not attributed to one person
proof: 54 countries, each with its own government, flag and story.
Over 2,000 languages: roughly a third of all the languages spoken on Earth.
Kenya alone speaks 40+ languages, and Sheng belongs to all of us.
posts.source: UN member states by region (un.org/en/about-us/member-states); Ethnologue, languages of Africa (ethnologue.com)
posts.caption:
"Africa is one country." No. 54 countries, 2,000+ languages, and Kenya alone speaks 40+.

Send this to the friend who says "I'm going to Africa" like it's one town.

#SetItStraight #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Some people still say Africa is one country.
That is *false*: Africa has 54 countries.
Africa speaks more than 2,000 languages.
It is one continent with *54 flags.*

posts.line: Hell's Gate is a Kenyan park you can *cycle* through.
posts.fact: Kenya Wildlife Service lets visitors walk and cycle past zebra, giraffe and buffalo, then hike the gorge.
posts.message: Hell's Gate in Naivasha is a Kenyan park you can explore on foot or by bike.
posts.source: Kenya Wildlife Service, Hell's Gate National Park (kws.go.ke)
beats: Hell's Gate is a Kenyan park you can *cycle* through.
You ride past zebra, giraffe and buffalo, then hike the gorge.
It is in Naivasha, about two hours from Nairobi.
posts.caption:
Hell's Gate, Naivasha: one of the few parks in Kenya you can explore by bike. Save this for your next weekend out.

#KenyaOnRecord #Naivasha
posts.action: Plan a day trip to Naivasha and hire a bike at the park gate
